| [LIT-031](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-031.md) v2 | Moving away from lexicalism in psycho- and neuro-linguistics | Krauska et al. (2023), DOI-10.3389/flang.2023.1125127. The authors argue that lemma-based production models encode two lexicalist assumptions: a morphology/syntax split, and a stored meaning–syntax–form "triad". | [LIT-046](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-046.md) v3 | The Computational Foundations of Collective Intelligence | Pilgrim et al. (2025), [ARXIV-2509.07999](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.07999). A conceptual framework, with no model, data or derivation. It then maps the collective's surplus onto familiar mechanisms (aggregation with noise σ_i²/n, distributional beliefs P(H), memory persistence T_c, division of labour). From it the authors derive 14 indicator properties: RPT-1–2, GWT-1–4, HOT-1–4, AST-1, PP-1 and AE-1–2. The claim for them is only that more of them raises the probability of consciousness. They assess a handful of systems against subsets of the list and conclude that no current system "appears to be a strong candidate". Transformer LLMs have "only a relatively weak case" for any GWT indicator, because a single forward pass has no recurrence or global broadcast. | [LIT-097](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-097.md) v3 | The Extended Mind | Clark & Chalmers (1998), DOI-10.1093/analys/58.1.7. The paper argues from a functionalist parity claim that a process or standing state which would count as cognitive if it happened in the head counts as cognitive when an external resource carries it, provided the resource is actively coupled to the organism here and now. Otto's notebook entry is its example of such a standing belief. From this it infers, in one paragraph, that the self extends too. The four "criteria" for a coupled resource (constancy, direct availability, automatic endorsement, and the admittedly "arguable" past conscious endorsement) are offered as the features that make the paradigm case clear. The paper explicitly says they are not necessary and sufficient conditions. | Active — read in full 2026-09-26 ([NOTE-180](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-180.md)); it is worth reading as the source text of the extended-mind thesis, and it is short. | [LIT-105](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-105.md) v3 | On the Evolution, Science, and Metaphysics of Consciousness | Veit (2025), DOI-10.1177/10597123251413204. Veit's reply to five commentaries on *A Philosophy for the Science of Animal Consciousness* (2023). Its main new content is the metaphysics the book left to one paragraph. He says hedonic "feel" is *identical* with a valence system: "a common currency of sharing evaluative information across multiple control systems". The currency metaphor, he says, is "not Cartesian but cybernetic" (p. 10). He keeps the word "qualia", arguing that Cartesians have no "definitional rights" (p. 9), and he insists the pathological complexity thesis (PCT) is compatible with any metaphysics, dualism and panpsychism included (p. 9). Against his other critics, he defends a bottom-up evolutionary method that uses human data (de Weerd); a naturalism that is neither autopoietic nor biopsychist (Sachs); evaluation-first over prediction-first, consciousness as an adaptation, and graded, partial unity (Suzuki); and the link to welfare science (Chincarini). | Active — read in full 2026-09-26 ([NOTE-187](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-187.md)); worth reading as the only extended statement of the metaphysics behind the pathological complexity thesis, and as the direct answer to Frankish ([LIT-103](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-103.md)). The reply to Frankish is the substantive part. The replies to de Weerd and Suzuki mostly restate the book's positions against objections quoted only in part, so read them alongside the commentaries. |

| [LIT-220](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-220.md) v2 | Real Patterns | Dennett (1991), DOI-10.2307/2027085. A pattern is real in some data "if there is a description of the data that is more efficient than the bit map, whether or not anyone can concoct it" (p. 34). This is Chaitin's incompressibility definition of randomness turned around (p. 32). Dennett uses the criterion, with the Game of Life's gliders and eaters as the stepping stone (pp. 37–42), to defend "mild realism" about beliefs. Folk psychology tracks a real, noisy pattern of enormous predictive leverage. Two rival interpretations can be "different, but equally real, patterns" with no deeper fact to settle between them (p. 49). | Active — read in full 2026-09-26 ([NOTE-190](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-190.md)); Worth reading as the source of the real-patterns criterion that rainforest realism generalises into a theory of existence, and as the paper whose exact definition the later literature modifies. It has a lossless-compression criterion, observer-relativity through "perspectives", and trade-offs between noise and simplicity. Its target is beliefs, not ontology in general. Dennett explicitly declines the label question ("I think that the view itself is clearer than either of the labels", p. 51). |
